title: One Publish control in the browser: the bound remote on Health, no URL typing per goal, docs and the UnAI live push

After child 1 the payload's remoteUrl may be null (bound remote) and the bound remote is served by `POST /repository/remote/read` (its live decoder lands with child 1).
- Health screen: apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ops-screens.tsx:180-206 `HealthScreen` (cr.health.root/banner/facts/verifier) - the project-level home for a "Repository" card; live-ops.tsx wires the ops reads.

- Live lane: UnAI (D:/projexts/UnAI), scripts/up.ps1; the owner's remote for UnAI is named by the owner at drive time (never invented).

FEATURE: the publish card becomes ONE control: when a remote is bound it shows "Publish to <remote>" with the landed commits it will push (from /runs/read landing) and a Publish arm/confirm sending {goalId, remoteUrl: null}; when no remote is bound it shows the URL input once (first binding) and sends {goalId, remoteUrl: <typed>}; a Change link on the card and on Health reveals the input again (the next publish rebinds); `moe.publish.remoteUrl` localStorage is gone; with nothing landed the card renders nothing. Health gains a "Repository" card: the bound remote (or "no remote bound - bind it from a goal's Publish card"), boundAt/boundBy, Change. README + runbook rewritten to the project shape.
definitionOfDone: goal-publish tests: bound remote -> no URL input, the card names the remote and the landed commits, Publish dispatches {goalId, remoteUrl: null} (payload asserted byte-exact through publish-port.ts); unbound -> the input renders once and Publish dispatches {goalId, remoteUrl: <typed>}; Change reveals the input while bound; nothing landed (no offer) -> the card renders nothing; `grep -rn "moe.publish.remoteUrl" apps/control-room/src` = 0 and no localStorage read/write remains in goal-publish.tsx.

If not, report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds naming it. (d) Record pre-change `Test Files N passed` for `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.

ADD THE MISSING READ CLIENT — the half of child 1's DoD 4 that did not land (task rail 1 forbids a DAEMON change; this is control-room work, which is this row's own domain, so absorb it rather than blocking). New apps/control-room/src/live/live-repository-remote.ts, following the shape of a sibling read client such as live-sessions.ts: POST `/repository/remote/read` with EXACTLY `{}`, and decode `{outcome:"REMOTE", remoteUrl, boundAt, boundBy}` with an EXACT-KEY record check — the same `exactDataRecord` discipline the other live clients use, which rejects a response whose key set differs rather than silently defaulting. `remoteUrl`, `boundAt` and `boundBy` are all NULL when unbound, so the decoder must accept null for each WITHOUT collapsing 'unbound' into 'malformed'. Add `/repository/remote/read` to apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts (the sorted list at :6-37). Test the decoder both ways: a bound frame, and an all-null unbound frame, plus a frame with an extra key which must be REFUSED.

ONE PUBLISH CONTROL, tests first. apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-publish.tsx (141 lines) today reads and writes `REMOTE_STORAGE_KEY = "moe.publish.remoteUrl"` through localStorage (:20, :31, :39) and gates `canPublish` on a typed URL (:75). Replace that with the bound remote: (a) BOUND -> no URL input; the card names the remote and the landed commits it will push (from /runs/read landing), and Publish dispatches `{goalId, remoteUrl: null}` — assert the payload BYTE-EXACT through publish-port.ts (22 lines, `submit(affordance, goalId, remoteUrl)`). (b) UNBOUND -> the input renders once and Publish dispatches `{goalId, remoteUrl: <typed>}`. (c) A Change link reveals the input while bound, and the next publish rebinds. (d) NOTHING LANDED (no offer) -> the card renders nothing at all; note `cr.publish.unoffered` exists today at :102 for the un-offered case, so decide and record whether that sentence stays or goes. (e) THE LOCALSTORAGE MUST BE GONE: `grep -rn 'moe.publish.remoteUrl' apps/control-room/src` = 0 and no localStorage read or write remains in goal-publish.tsx. That grep is DoD 1's own gate — a leftover write would keep a stale URL shadowing the bound remote.

THE REPOSITORY CARD ON HEALTH, and a SIZE CHECK FIRST. apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ops-screens.tsx is 228 lines TODAY against the row's own 250-line ceiling (DoD 5), and this step adds a card — measure with `wc -l` BEFORE writing, and if the addition would cross 250, extract the Health screen (or the new card) into its own module in the same step rather than discovering the violation at the final gate. Then the card itself: the bound remote with boundAt/boundBy from the real `/repository/remote/read` frame, the unbound wording ('no remote bound - bind it from a goal's Publish card') when null, and a Change control. Wire the read into the ops poller in live-ops.tsx beside the existing sessions/policy/health reads (:9-16), and update whatever roster or poller test pins that set — a read added to the screen but not the poller renders once and never refreshes.

THE BROWSER JOURNEY over a REAL daemon, in tests/e2e/control-room/ (follow the harness in daemon-board.spec.ts / prd-to-approval.spec.ts). Land a commit -> the Publish card appears -> the FIRST publish types the URL, using a LOCAL BARE REPOSITORY as the remote so the lane pushes somewhere real without touching anyone's account -> the receipt link renders -> a SECOND goal publishes with NO typing, which is the whole point of the feature and the arm that proves the remote was bound rather than remembered per goal. Capture the control-room fixtures this row uses FROM THAT RUN (task rail 2: exact-key decoders reject hand-written frames, so a synthetic fixture fails at the decoder and reads as a test bug). Quote the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line.

THE LIVE PUSH ON UnAI (DoD 4, and task rail 2). At D:/projexts/UnAI via scripts/up.ps1: bind THE OWNER'S remote by the first publish from the browser — NEVER invent a URL and never one carrying a credential — then record in a row comment under ~4500 chars: the `moe-publish-receipt/1` PUSHED line with the remote branch link, and then a SECOND publish with no URL typed, with its receipt id. A REFUSED push is recorded VERBATIM with its code and is a legitimate outcome; it is never worked around and never retried into a fabricated success. If the owner has not named a remote for UnAI, say so and record the refusal or the unbound state instead of guessing one — an invented remote is the one failure here that could push real code somewhere unintended.

comments.author: worker-cceb207f
comments.content:
FROM task-9d55341928f04110ba7b286a985f8fa0 (child 1b, now in REVIEW): the daemon route your decoder and proxy pins consume is LANDED. Everything below is measured at the delivered tree, not designed.

PATH + METHOD: `POST /repository/remote/read`, body EXACTLY `{}` (an empty request body also forwards). Exported as `REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PATH` from apps/daemon/src/http/repository-remote-read.ts:21. Capability gate: CAPABILITIES.GOAL — the same gate as /goals/source/read.

SUCCESS SHAPE, exact 5-key roster, nothing more and nothing less:
  { boundAt: string | null, boundBy: string | null, outcome: "REMOTE", readAt: string, remoteUrl: string | null }
HTTP status 200. `boundBy` is a PRINCIPAL id (e.g. "principal-1"), never a credential. `readAt` is the daemon's composition clock. All three nullable fields are null TOGETHER or set TOGETHER — there is no partial state.

REFUSALS your decoder must handle. All three arrive as HTTP 200 with an `outcome: "REFUSED"` body carrying `code` and `layer`, where layer is always the string "REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ":
  REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_CAPABILITY_DENIED   — credential lacks the GOAL capability
  REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_PROJECT_MISMATCH    — credential bound to a different project
  REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_UNREADABLE          — see the WARNING below; rarer than it looks
Exported as the frozen roster `REPOSITORY_REMOTE_READ_CODES` (same module) in that order.

LISTENER refusals, which do NOT carry a layer and are NOT 200:
  LISTENER_REPOSITORY_REMOTE_REQUEST_INVALID — HTTP 400; any non-POST method, or any body that is not `{}`/empty
  LISTENER_REPOSITORY_REMOTE_UNAVAILABLE     — HTTP 503; the port is not wired
Both are in LISTENER_REFUSAL_CODES with statusFor 400/503 (http-listener-guards.ts:86-87, :216-217).

**WARNING, THE NON-OBVIOUS PART — do not build a "store is broken" branch.** `readProjectRemote` catches its OWN store failure and re-applies today's url admission rule on the read. So a broken store, an undecodable binding, AND a url that `admitRemoteUrl` no longer admits ALL come back as the UNBOUND view — all nulls under `outcome: "REMOTE"` — not as a refusal. UNREADABLE is reachable only when an injected reader throws, which production never does. This is child 1's deliberate fail-closed rule (surfacing a superseded remote would point a push at a repository the operator has already left). CONSEQUENCE FOR YOUR UI: render an all-nulls view as "no remote yet" and nothing else; a "cannot read the remote" state would be dead code. I found this by probe during adversarial review — my own module comment had it wrong — and it is now pinned by the arm `reads an unreadable STORE as unbound, not as a refusal` in apps/daemon/src/http/repository-remote-read.test.ts.

YOUR PROXY PIN — THIS ONE REDS UNTIL YOU DO IT. The route is deliberately recorded as NOT dev-proxied, because apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts is YOUR path and this row is a pure daemon leaf. I added "/repository/remote/read" to `UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS` in apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts:91-101 (with a comment naming your row). That census is an EXACT set-equality assertion, so when you add the path to DEV_PROXY_PATHS you MUST delete it from UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS in the same change — otherwise that arm reds with the entry outliving its gap. Also note apps/control-room/src/live/live-document-proxy.test.ts:6 asserts DEV_PROXY_PATHS with hard-coded literals via toStrictEqual, so it needs the new literal too. Until you land the proxy the route works in production and fails ONLY under the dev server, which is where the e2e lane runs.

A working consumer to copy: apps/control-room/src/live/live-sessions.ts is the sessions read's decoder and uses the identical envelope. My route mirrors sessions-read.ts line for line, so its decoder shape transfers directly.

comments.author: worker-12c76c19
comments.content:
FROM SPIDR CHILD 2 (task-f6f33a3925bf4856b42cf84a37bb0f9e), which gates the publish OFFER — read before planning the Publish control.

WHAT CHANGED, and what it means for your row. `/affordances/read` no longer mints `repository.publish` for every activated goal. It is offered ONLY when at least one node of that goal carries a landing receipt with `outcome === "COMMITTED"`. A goal with no landing, or whose landings are all REFUSED, gets NO publish offer at all.

CONSEQUENCE FOR YOUR CONTROL: `apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-publish.tsx:49` finds its offer by `row["commandKind"] === "repository.publish" && row["targetAggregateId"] === \`publish:${goalId}\``. For an unlanded goal that find now returns undefined, so the Publish card renders nothing — which is the intended end state ("the card then renders nothing — child 3"). You do NOT need to add a "nothing is landed" branch to the card: the absent offer already is that branch. `board-header.tsx:23` keys on the same presence and will likewise stop pointing at the card. NO offer SHAPE changed — same commandKind, same `publish:<goalId>` target, same envelope — so nothing in your rendering path needs re-keying.

THE SURFACE ARM THAT PINS IT, if you want a fixture to copy: `apps/daemon/src/repository/goal-landing-facts.test.ts`, describe "the publish offer on /affordances/read", arm **"APPEARS targeting publish:<goalId> once a commit lands, and goes again on a fresh world"**. It reads the real surface through `createAffordancePort` and asserts set-equality on `commandKind@target` for the goal's two aggregates:
- before any landing: `["goal.close@goal-1"]`
- after `seedReviewAcceptance(store, "node-a")` + `seedLandingReceipt(store, "node-a", "COMMITTED")`: `["goal.close@goal-1", "repository.publish@publish:goal-1"]`
Sibling arms pin that a REFUSED-only landing stays unoffered, and that a COMMITTED landing on a node outside the goal's graph does not count.

ONE FIXTURE GOTCHA THAT COST ME A STEP: the seed world's activated graph names node **`node-a`**, NOT `node-1` (the plan asserted `node-1` and was wrong — probe output in comment-6d272018 on my row). If you build a browser fixture that needs a landed goal, seed `node-a`. `node-1` is useful as the opposite: a real landable node the goal's graph does not carry.

`goal.close` is unaffected in every arm — task-8145137c's NO_CONTRACT rule for the seed/Foundation journey is untouched, so the close card's behaviour is exactly what it was.
